symbols.name: createAIChatStream
signatures: (adapter: AIChatAdapter, request: AIChatRequest, options?: AIChatStreamOptions | undefined): ReadableStream<any>
symbols.summary:
Shared send lifecycle for HTTP, custom and SDK consumers. Snapshots the request
before returning, starts lazily on demand, requires finish followed by EOF,
rejects events after finish, and forwards abort to the adapter even during a read.
Cancellation settles promptly; an adapter must honor its signal to release I/O.
Iterator cleanup is requested, but never awaited behind an uncooperative next().
No storage, retry, resumption, tool execution or browser/SDK dependency.

signatures: (options: AIChatHTTPOptions): AIChatAdapter
symbols.summary:
HTTP adapter for an application endpoint serving AI SDK UI Message Streams.
Posts UIMessage history, submit-message trigger and optional explicit tools/parameters.
The endpoint owns its SDK model/provider and consumes those extra fields if supported.
No provider SDK dependency, tool execution or automatic retry is introduced. Text,
structured data parts, tool calls/results, metadata and explicit finish are normalized.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Tool schemas are application-owned, synchronous JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12.
Schemas are compiled on construction using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion,
defaults and property removal disabled. The registered action validator still runs.
No schema, handler, permission or output type is inferred from a TypeScript type.
Only mapOutput results are returned; registry metadata, errors and causes stay local.
The bridge reads the current registration at call time and rejects results if that
action was replaced during execution. Context lifetime checks are owned by the registry.
Duplicate call IDs (including failed calls) are rejected for this bridge's lifetime.
This is local retry protection, not durable idempotency or server authorization.
JSON schemas, arguments and projected outputs must be plain finite JSON data, at most
64 levels deep, 10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters per value.
Creating a bridge does not expose data externally or contact an AI service.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createAjvValidator
signatures: (options?: AjvValidatorOptions | undefined): ((schema: object, data: unknown, overrides?: any) => { valid: boolean; errors: {}; rawErrors?: {} | undefined; }) & { ajv: any; }
symbols.summary: Creates an Ajv-based validator.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options.locale - Error message language ('ja' | 'en'). Uses Ajv default messages if omitted.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not modify schemas after compilation; provide a new schema object instead.
The returned ajv instance corresponds to the default draft. Specify draft explicitly when using addSchema/addKeyword.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

symbols.name: createExecutionSession
signatures: (options?: { readonly historyLimit?: number | undefined; } | undefined): ExecutionSession
symbols.summary:
Creates a framework-independent execution session (default history limit 50, max 1000).
One operation runs at a time. cancel changes status to cancelling and aborts its signal;
it does not race the promise or unlock a handler that ignores cancellation. A handler
resolving after cancellation is recorded as succeeded with cancelRequested=true.
Only an AbortError after a cancellation request is recorded as cancelled. Other errors
remain failures. Late progress updates are ignored. Observers cannot break execution.

History contains bounded labels/progress only, not inputs, results or exception details.
It is transient UI state, not an audit log or durable deduplication. Applications must
handle server authorization, idempotency and uncertain commit outcomes themselves.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createGenerativeUIContract
signatures: (components: {}): GenerativeUIContract
symbols.summary: Builds a provider-neutral draft-07 response schema from explicit component definitions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Up to 32 unique type names, each with an inline object-root dataSchema. References,
IDs, anchors, dialect declarations and async schemas are rejected (including nested
reserved keys); this prevents reference rebasing and mixed-dialect ambiguity when
schemas are composed. No network loading occurs. Schemas are snapshotted/frozen and
compiled immediately using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion/defaults/removal
disabled. Invalid schemas throw configuration errors.
Exported schema describes structural constraints; runtime validation additionally
enforces unique block IDs and JSON size/depth limits. Custom business validators and
authorization still belong to the app. Provider-specific schema subsets may require
an application adapter; this function never contacts an AI service.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createOpenAICompatibleChatAdapter
signatures: (options: OpenAICompatibleChatOptions): AIChatAdapter
symbols.summary:
OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions HTTP/SSE adapter. Uses one choice, assembles tool
argument fragments before emitting a call and preserves tool result history. Incomplete
streams and invalid tool JSON fail instead of pretending completion. No tool is run.
Arbitrary native data parts are not sent to this text/tool protocol. Provider-specific
model/schema support remains explicit through parameters; capabilities are transport-level.

symbols.name: defineActionTool
signatures: <TInput, TOutput>(definition: ActionToolDefinition<TInput, TOutput>): DefinedActionTool<TInput, TOutput>
symbols.summary: Defines a typed Action and Tool using one input schema and parser.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
This does not register or expose anything. Schema validation also runs for direct
registry.executeAction calls, before the mandatory typed parser. No TypeScript type
is asserted from JSON Schema alone. Schemas use the bridge's synchronous draft-07 /
2020-12 support and bounded immutable JSON snapshots; no coercion/default insertion.
Parser failures and exceptions become a fixed input error. A parser may refine or
transform validated data; it must be synchronous. mapOutput still validates unknown
output because registry IDs are replaceable. Provider schemas/transport remain host-owned.

symbols.name: prepareProposalBatch
signatures: <TRecord extends Record<string, any> = Record<string, any>>(entries: {}, validateCandidate?: ProposalBatchValidator<TRecord> | undefined): PreparedProposalBatch<TRecord>
symbols.summary:
Prepares every selected record before a multi-record apply starts.
Reuses single-proposal decisions, before/version checks and candidate validation.
Duplicate proposal IDs anywhere and duplicate selected target IDs fail closed.
Every selected proposal needs all fields decided and at least one accepted change.
Exclude all-rejected proposals explicitly. Empty selection is not executable.

Pass proposals already validated with validateProposalInput. This is not an external
input parser, cross-record business validator, database transaction or authorization
boundary. Payload candidates are shallow immutable snapshots, like buildApplyPayload.

symbols.name: validateGenerativeUIDocument
signatures: (input: unknown): GenerativeUIDocumentResult
symbols.summary: Validates and snapshots a fully assembled UI document without a UI dependency.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Requires version 1, a document ID, and at most 32 flat blocks with unique IDs.
Blocks have exactly id/type/data; the envelope has exactly version/id/blocks.
Data must be an object. Component names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`.
All values must be plain finite JSON data: no accessors, functions, cycles,
sparse arrays, class instances or undefined. Limits: 64 nesting levels,
10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters for the entire document.
The successful result is cloned and recursively frozen; caller input is untouched.
This validates structure, not business data or authorization. Unknown component
names are allowed here and handled by the application's explicit UI registry.
Parse provider JSON and assemble streaming fragments before calling this function.

tags.name: example

signatures: <TRecord extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>>(input: unknown, options: ValidateProposalOptions<TRecord>): ProposalValidationResult<TRecord>
symbols.summary: Validates external input and constructs a safe RecordProposal<TRecord>.

tags.name: param

symbols.name: verifyCurrentState
signatures: <TRecord extends Record<string, any> = Record<string, any>>(currentRecord: TRecord, currentVersion: string | number, proposal: RecordProposal<TRecord>, decisions: Readonly<Partial<Record<Extract<keyof TRecord, string>, FieldDecision>>>): ConsistencyCheckResult<TRecord>
symbols.summary:
Verifies consistency between the current source data/version and the proposal content.

1. Version match: Verifies strict equality between proposal.baseVersion and currentVersion.
2. Before-value match: For accepted fields, verifies whether the current value strictly matches the proposal's before value
   (detecting value discrepancies caused by unsaved manual edits in forms, etc.).

Tool schemas are application-owned, synchronous JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Up to 32 unique type names, each with an inline object-root dataSchema. References,
IDs, anchors, dialect declarations and async schemas are rejected (including nested
reserved keys); this prevents reference rebasing and mixed-dialect ambiguity when
schemas are composed. No network loading occurs. Schemas are snapshotted/frozen and
compiled immediately using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion/defaults/removal
disabled. Invalid schemas throw configuration errors.
Exported schema describes structural constraints; runtime validation additionally
enforces unique block IDs and JSON size/depth limits. Custom business validators and
authorization still belong to the app. Provider-specific schema subsets may require
an application adapter; this function never contacts an AI service.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Requires version 1, a document ID, and at most 32 flat blocks with unique IDs.
Blocks have exactly id/type/data; the envelope has exactly version/id/blocks.
Data must be an object. Component names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`.
All values must be plain finite JSON data: no accessors, functions, cycles,
sparse arrays, class instances or undefined. Limits: 64 nesting levels,
10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters for the entire document.
The successful result is cloned and recursively frozen; caller input is untouched.
This validates structure, not business data or authorization. Unknown component
names are allowed here and handled by the application's explicit UI registry.
Parse provider JSON and assemble streaming fragments before calling this function.

Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.

not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not mutate the schema object after compilation; pass a new object instead.
The returned `ajv` property is the instance for the default draft. When using addSchema/addKeyword, specify the draft explicitly.

keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

symbols.summary:
Generates a Zod validation schema from a JSONSchema.

Produces appropriate Zod validators according to property type/format,
applying implemented JSON Schema constraints and supported x-zod extensions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Partial conversion, not a JSON Schema evaluator. additionalProperties, type
unions and positive multipleOf are supported. Exclusive bounds, composition,
references and advanced array constraints are not generally preserved. format: date only
checks string type. Use createAjvValidator at the authoritative JSON boundary.
Only implemented x-zod options take effect; declarations do not imply support.
Root/nested required entries are checked even without properties declarations;
enum applies at the root as well as to nested values.
Declared/required __proto__ properties are rejected at conversion time.

and protected from concurrent untrusted filesystem mutation.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Tool schemas are application-owned, synchronous JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12.
Schemas are compiled on construction using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion,
defaults and property removal disabled. The registered action validator still runs.
No schema, handler, permission or output type is inferred from a TypeScript type.
Only mapOutput results are returned; registry metadata, errors and causes stay local.
The bridge reads the current registration at call time and rejects results if that
action was replaced during execution. Context lifetime checks are owned by the registry.
Duplicate call IDs (including failed calls) are rejected for this bridge's lifetime.
This is local retry protection, not durable idempotency or server authorization.
JSON schemas, arguments and projected outputs must be plain finite JSON data, at most
64 levels deep, 10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters per value.
Creating a bridge does not expose data externally or contact an AI service.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createExecutionSession
signatures: (options?: { readonly historyLimit?: number | undefined; } | undefined): ExecutionSession
symbols.summary:
Creates a framework-independent execution session (default history limit 50, max 1000).
One operation runs at a time. cancel changes status to cancelling and aborts its signal;
it does not race the promise or unlock a handler that ignores cancellation. A handler
resolving after cancellation is recorded as succeeded with cancelRequested=true.
Only an AbortError after a cancellation request is recorded as cancelled. Other errors
remain failures. Late progress updates are ignored. Observers cannot break execution.

History contains bounded labels/progress only, not inputs, results or exception details.
It is transient UI state, not an audit log or durable deduplication. Applications must
handle server authorization, idempotency and uncertain commit outcomes themselves.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createGenerativeUIContract
signatures: (components: {}): GenerativeUIContract
symbols.summary: Builds a provider-neutral draft-07 response schema from explicit component definitions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Up to 32 unique type names, each with an inline object-root dataSchema. References,
IDs, anchors, dialect declarations and async schemas are rejected (including nested
reserved keys); this prevents reference rebasing and mixed-dialect ambiguity when
schemas are composed. No network loading occurs. Schemas are snapshotted/frozen and
compiled immediately using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion/defaults/removal
disabled. Invalid schemas throw configuration errors.
Exported schema describes structural constraints; runtime validation additionally
enforces unique block IDs and JSON size/depth limits. Custom business validators and
authorization still belong to the app. Provider-specific schema subsets may require
an application adapter; this function never contacts an AI service.

tags.name: example

symbols.summary:
OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions HTTP/SSE adapter. Uses one choice, assembles tool
argument fragments before emitting a call and preserves tool result history. Incomplete
streams and invalid tool JSON fail instead of pretending completion. No tool is run.
Arbitrary native data parts are not sent to this text/tool protocol. Provider-specific
model/schema support remains explicit through parameters; capabilities are transport-level.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
This does not register or expose anything. Schema validation also runs for direct
registry.executeAction calls, before the mandatory typed parser. No TypeScript type
is asserted from JSON Schema alone. Schemas use the bridge's synchronous draft-07 /
2020-12 support and bounded immutable JSON snapshots; no coercion/default insertion.
Parser failures and exceptions become a fixed input error. A parser may refine or
transform validated data; it must be synchronous. mapOutput still validates unknown
output because registry IDs are replaceable. Provider schemas/transport remain host-owned.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Requires version 1, a document ID, and at most 32 flat blocks with unique IDs.
Blocks have exactly id/type/data; the envelope has exactly version/id/blocks.
Data must be an object. Component names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`.
All values must be plain finite JSON data: no accessors, functions, cycles,
sparse arrays, class instances or undefined. Limits: 64 nesting levels,
10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters for the entire document.
The successful result is cloned and recursively frozen; caller input is untouched.
This validates structure, not business data or authorization. Unknown component
names are allowed here and handled by the application's explicit UI registry.
Parse provider JSON and assemble streaming fragments before calling this function.

symbols.name: castValuesBySchema
signatures: (values: any, schema: JSONSchemaProperty, options?: SchemaCastOptions | undefined): any
symbols.summary:
Convert form values, separately from JSON Schema validation. Never adds defaults,
resolves $ref, selects composition branches, or coerces booleans/dates/null values.
Numeric empty strings become null for nullable numeric types, otherwise undefined.
Legacy numeric parsing intentionally accepts prefixes and truncates integers.
Mismatched object/array values and unconvertible strings are retained for validation.
Walks only own declared properties, prefixItems and items; unknown properties survive.
Does not mutate inputs. Throws beyond depth 64 or 10,000 visited values (including cycles).

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not mutate the schema object after compilation; pass a new object instead.
The returned `ajv` property is the instance for the default draft. When using addSchema/addKeyword, specify the draft explicitly.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

Generates a Zod validation schema from a JSONSchema.

Produces appropriate Zod validators according to property type/format,
applying implemented JSON Schema constraints and supported x-zod extensions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Partial conversion, not a JSON Schema evaluator. additionalProperties, type
unions and positive multipleOf are supported. Exclusive bounds, composition,
references and advanced array constraints are not generally preserved. format: date only
checks string type. Use createAjvValidator at the authoritative JSON boundary.
Only implemented x-zod options take effect; declarations do not imply support.
Root/nested required entries are checked even without properties declarations;
enum applies at the root as well as to nested values.
Declared/required __proto__ properties are rejected at conversion time.

symbols.summary:
Convert form values, separately from JSON Schema validation. Never adds defaults,
resolves $ref, selects composition branches, or coerces booleans/dates/null values.
Numeric empty strings become null for nullable numeric types, otherwise undefined.
Legacy numeric parsing intentionally accepts prefixes and truncates integers.
Mismatched object/array values and unconvertible strings are retained for validation.
Walks only own declared properties, prefixItems and items; unknown properties survive.
Does not mutate inputs. Throws beyond depth 64 or 10,000 visited values (including cycles).

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not mutate the schema object after compilation; pass a new object instead.
The returned `ajv` property is the instance for the default draft. When using addSchema/addKeyword, specify the draft explicitly.

keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

symbols.name: ContainedPathRoot
symbols.summary:
Pins a trusted root (including a not-yet-created root) to an absolute physical
path. Every operation rejects symlinks in that path and below it, including
dangling links. An initial root alias is resolved once at construction.

This is server-only. The root and its ancestors must not be concurrently
renamed or modified by untrusted OS users: portable Node path APIs cannot
provide an atomic openat-style directory walk. Hard links are also outside
this boundary; provision an application-owned directory with suitable ACLs.

symbols.name: planGanttTasks
signatures: <T extends GanttPlanningTask>(tasks: {}, dependencies: {}, options?: GanttSchedulingOptions | undefined): GanttScheduleResult<T>
symbols.summary:
Plan whole working days with a shared calendar and optional resource capacities.
Dates must be local midnight (date-only strings are parsed locally). Finishes are
exclusive next-working-day boundaries. A positive span with no working days gets
one day; durationDays overrides inferred duration, including zero-day milestones.

Stable topological/input order decides resource precedence. Tasks are never split,
pulled before their input starts, or optimized for shortest makespan. All statuses
participate; actual/frozen work and individual resource calendars are not modeled.
Summary rows are preserved but excluded from planning. Invalid inputs, cycles,
over-capacity demand and exhausted search bounds throw without mutating inputs.
CPM is dependency-only BEFORE leveling; capacity delays are reported separately.

symbols.name: scheduleGanttTasks

symbols.summary:
Apply FS/SS/FF/SF constraints in topological order, moving successors forward only.
Preserves each task's calendar-day duration and time-of-day using local date arithmetic.
Input tasks/links are not mutated. Cycles, missing IDs and summary dependencies throw.
A third options argument opts into the local-midnight day planner with working calendars
and optional capacity leveling. Omit it to preserve legacy time-of-day behavior.

symbols.name: planGanttTasks
signatures: <T extends GanttPlanningTask>(tasks: {}, dependencies: {}, options?: GanttSchedulingOptions | undefined): GanttScheduleResult<T>
symbols.summary:
Plan whole working days with a shared calendar and optional resource capacities.
Dates must be local midnight (date-only strings are parsed locally). Finishes are
exclusive next-working-day boundaries. A positive span with no working days gets
one day; durationDays overrides inferred duration, including zero-day milestones.

Stable topological/input order decides resource precedence. Tasks are never split,
pulled before their input starts, or optimized for shortest makespan. All statuses
participate; actual/frozen work and individual resource calendars are not modeled.
Summary rows are preserved but excluded from planning. Invalid inputs, cycles,
over-capacity demand and exhausted search bounds throw without mutating inputs.
CPM is dependency-only BEFORE leveling; capacity delays are reported separately.

symbols.name: scheduleGanttTasks
signatures: <T extends GanttPlanningTask>(tasks: {}, dependencies: {}, options?: GanttSchedulingOptions | undefined): {}
symbols.summary:
Apply FS/SS/FF/SF constraints in topological order, moving successors forward only.
Preserves each task's calendar-day duration and time-of-day using local date arithmetic.
Input tasks/links are not mutated. Cycles, missing IDs and summary dependencies throw.
A third options argument opts into the local-midnight day planner with working calendars
and optional capacity leveling. Omit it to preserve legacy time-of-day behavior.

symbols.name: resolveSealLabel
signatures: (fullName?: string | undefined, options?: SealLabelOptions | undefined): string
symbols.summary:
Resolves the label (typically family name) to display on a fallback seal.

Priority order:
1. `options.sealLabel`
2. `options.familyName`
3. `fullName` parsing (applying `nameOrder` rule)

When `nameOrder: "auto"`:
- Names containing CJK characters: use first token
- 2 or more Latin words: use last token
- Otherwise: use first token

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
resolveSealLabel("山田 太郎") // => "山田"
resolveSealLabel("John Smith") // => "Smith"
resolveSealLabel("TANAKA", { maxChars: 2 }) // => "TA"
```

signatures: (options?: JapaneseHolidayCalendarOptions | undefined): (parts: JapaneseCalendarDate) => boolean
symbols.summary:
Selects a Japanese calendar provider and snapshots exact-date closure overrides.
holiday-jp is recommended and remains the default; calculated mode is a 2022–2099
planning calendar with approximate equinox defaults and no historical special moves.
Recreate a provider after updating its configuration; no announcements are fetched.
Dataset selection changes behavior, not installed dependencies. The pure calculated
subpath is available separately and does not load holiday-jp at runtime.

symbols.name: getCalculatedJapaneseHolidays
signatures: (year: number, equinoxDays?: JapaneseEquinoxDays | undefined): {}
symbols.summary:
Calculates Japanese holidays under the ordinary rules in effect from 2022.
Includes fixed dates, Happy Monday rules, Sunday substitutes and citizens' holidays.
Equinox defaults use a linear/leap-year approximation, not an astronomical ephemeris
or official announcement. Supply announced days when official dates are required.
Excludes historical special moves (including 2020/2021) and future one-off laws.

tags.name: param
tags.text: year Integer, 2022–2099; unsupported years throw RangeError.

tags.name: param
tags.text: equinoxDays Optional announced March/September days, each 19–24.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Fresh sorted holiday records. Predicted dates require official verification.

symbols.name: resolveSealLabel
signatures: (fullName?: string | undefined, options?: SealLabelOptions | undefined): string
symbols.summary:
Resolves the label (typically family name) to display on a fallback seal.

Priority order:
1. `options.sealLabel`
2. `options.familyName`
3. `fullName` parsing (applying `nameOrder` rule)

When `nameOrder: "auto"`:
- Names containing CJK characters: use first token
- 2 or more Latin words: use last token
- Otherwise: use first token

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
resolveSealLabel("山田 太郎") // => "山田"
resolveSealLabel("John Smith") // => "Smith"
resolveSealLabel("TANAKA", { maxChars: 2 }) // => "TA"
```

symbols.name: ContainedPathRoot
symbols.summary:
Pins a trusted root (including a not-yet-created root) to an absolute physical
path. Every operation rejects symlinks in that path and below it, including
dangling links. An initial root alias is resolved once at construction.

This is server-only. The root and its ancestors must not be concurrently
renamed or modified by untrusted OS users: portable Node path APIs cannot
provide an atomic openat-style directory walk. Hard links are also outside
this boundary; provision an application-owned directory with suitable ACLs.

symbols.name: LocalStorageAdapter
symbols.summary:
Storage adapter for the local filesystem.

Used to store files on the local disk instead of cloud storage
during development and testing.

## Features
- Uses Node.js `fs/promises`
- Automatic directory creation
- Automatic MIME type detection
- Recursive file listing

Keys must be relative paths without dot segments or backslashes. Symlinks
below the pinned root are rejected. The directory and its ancestors must be
owned by the application and protected from concurrent untrusted mutation.

symbols.name: USFederalHoliday
symbols.summary: A federal holiday occurrence. Both dates use YYYY-MM-DD without a timezone.

symbols.name: USFederalHolidayOptions
symbols.summary: Configure federal observance and explicit application closures; exclusions take precedence.

symbols.name: USHolidayAddition
symbols.summary: An application-selected closure date; used exactly as supplied without automatic shifting.

symbols.name: US_BUSINESS_DEFAULTS
symbols.summary: US presentation settings; currency does not imply a tax policy or timezone.

symbols.name: createUSFederalHolidayCalendar
signatures: (options?: USFederalHolidayOptions | undefined): (parts: USCalendarDate) => boolean
symbols.summary:
Creates a civil-date provider using a snapshot of application calendar overrides.
Use this for announced one-off closures or company policy without changing the
built-in federal rules. No external service is polled and no announcement is inferred.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options Observance mode, added closures and excluded dates; exclusions win.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A structurally compatible data-engine HolidayCalendar; months are zero-based.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for invalid override dates; TypeError for unnamed additions.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: formatUSD
signatures: (amount: number): string
symbols.summary:
Formats a finite USD amount in dollars using en-US and two fractional digits.
Presentation uses Intl rounding, not an accounting calculation or currency conversion.

tags.name: param
tags.text: amount Amount in dollars (1.25 means $1.25), including negative credits.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for NaN or infinite amounts.

symbols.name: formatUSDate
signatures: (date: Date, timeZone: string): string
symbols.summary:
Formats an instant as an en-US numeric date in an explicitly selected timezone.
The United States has multiple timezones; this API has no host-local default.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date Valid Date representing an instant; civil date strings are not accepted.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone Intl timezone identifier, for example America/New_York or UTC.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Month/day/year text in the supplied timezone.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for an invalid Date or timezone; TypeError if timezone is absent.

symbols.name: getUSFederalHolidays
signatures: (year: number, options?: USFederalHolidayOptions | undefined): {}
symbols.summary:
Lists the eleven recurring nationwide federal holidays under the current rules.
Observed mode (default) moves Saturday to Friday and Sunday to Monday for a
standard Monday–Friday schedule. Results are filtered by selected date, including
next January's New Year's Day when observed in December of the requested year.
Excludes state/local holidays, Inauguration Day and one-off executive closures.
Additional dates are used exactly as supplied and replace labels on matching
selected dates. Exclusions run last. No remote data is fetched.
This is a planning policy, not a private-employer working-day determination.
Source: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/

tags.name: param
tags.text: year Calendar year from 2021 through 2099. Future rules can change.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options Observance mode plus explicit additional or excluded closure dates.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Fresh date-sorted records whose selected date falls within year.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for unsupported years or invalid override dates; TypeError for unnamed additions.

symbols.name: usFederalHolidayCalendar
signatures: ({ year, month, day }: USCalendarDate): boolean
symbols.summary:
Tests a civil date against the standard observed federal holiday calendar.
Structurally compatible with data-engine's HolidayCalendar; no engine dependency.

tags.name: param
tags.text: parts Civil date with zero-based month; the caller converts instants to its timezone.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Whether the civil date is an observed federal holiday.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for an invalid civil date or year outside 2021–2099.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { usFederalHolidayCalendar } from '@alneas/appkit-core/us';
usFederalHolidayCalendar({ year: 2026, month: 6, day: 3 }); // true

symbols.name: USBusinessDocumentInput
symbols.summary: Explicit inputs for a renderer-neutral USD document. Line amounts are precomputed dollars.

symbols.name: USBusinessDocumentModel
symbols.summary: Portable document model for a host renderer. This value is not a PDF binary.

symbols.name: USDocumentType
signatures: export type USDocumentType = 'quote' | 'invoice' | 'creditNote';
symbols.summary: Supported US business document presets; no tax or electronic-invoice profile is inferred.

symbols.name: US_LETTER_PAGE
symbols.summary: US Letter portrait dimensions in PDF points (72 points per inch), with half-inch margins.

symbols.name: createUSBusinessDocument
signatures: (input: USBusinessDocumentInput): USBusinessDocumentModel
symbols.summary:
Assembles a USD quote, invoice or credit-note model using generic engine calculation.
A host owns rendering/export, fonts and safe text handling; no PDF library is loaded.
Supply precomputed line amounts and explicit tax/rounding policy. Uses JavaScript
numbers, not exact decimal accounting or automatic tax determination. Credit notes
use positive magnitudes and require an original invoice reference; ledger signs
remain caller-owned. Civil due dates are never shifted by a holiday calendar.

tags.name: param
tags.text: input Document fields, precomputed dollar line amounts and explicit tax policy.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: English template, US Letter geometry, engine data, amounts and formatted values.

tags.name: throws
tags.text:
TypeError for missing required text/credit reference; RangeError for invalid dates,
negative/nonfinite amounts, invalid rate or invalid output from the supplied rounder.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createUSDocumentTemplate
signatures: (documentType: USDocumentType): BusinessDocumentTemplate
symbols.summary:
Creates a fresh, customizable English quote/invoice/credit-note engine template.
No Japanese seals, legacy summary tables, font assumptions or tax defaults are enabled.

tags.name: param
tags.text: documentType quote, invoice or creditNote; unknown values throw TypeError.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Independent BusinessDocumentTemplate with English line columns and labels.

tags.name: example
